guide.introBody: A business system does not automatically improve efficiency simply because it is introduced. If its design does not fit the work, input screens are too complex, permissions are unclear, or post-launch support is insufficient, the finished system may go unused.

insights.title: Workflow
insights.body: Clarify who makes which decisions and when, and document exception handling as well as the standard flow.

insights.title: Data
insights.body: Review input fields, history, search criteria, existing-data migration, and inconsistent notation in advance so the data is usable after implementation.

insights.title: Adoption
insights.body: Define training, permissions, a support contact, and an improvement cycle so staff can continue using the system.

guide.tipsLead: Rather than building every feature from the outset, we recommend starting small in an area likely to show results and improving it while observing staff response.

tips.title: Define the goal as an operational improvement, not a feature
tips.body: Before naming features such as customer management or reservation management, clarify what the feature should improve.
points: Reduce missed or overlooked inquiries
Share each team member's interaction history
Shorten the time needed to prepare estimates and invoices
Make follow-up timing visible

tips.title: Interview staff about exception handling
tips.body: Review processes outside the standard flow in advance, such as returns, cancellations, reassignment, duplicate registration, and temporary permission changes.
points: Processes that occur only at month-end or during busy periods
Amounts and conditions that require approval
Who corrects input errors or duplicate records
Permission changes after resignation or internal transfer

tips.title: Decide early how to handle existing data
tips.body: When migrating data accumulated in Excel, paper records, or a legacy system, define the migration scope, duplicates, notation inconsistencies, and reviewer in advance.
points: Which data to migrate
How many years of historical data to migrate
How to resolve duplicates and inconsistent notation
How long to retain old data

tips.title: Roll out in phases instead of building everything at once
tips.body: Observe staff response to the first release and apply it to the next improvement. Detecting gaps in the requirements early is important.
points: Document the current workflow and challenges
Choose 1 operation with high potential impact
Run a pilot with the minimum necessary features
Review priorities before adding features

tips.title: Clarify permissions and responsibilities
tips.body: Clarify who can view, edit, and approve. Ambiguous permissions can cause information leaks and operational mistakes.
points: Allowed operations by department and role
Minimize the number of administrators
Approval flow and responsible person
Permission-change procedure for resignation or transfer

tips.title: Provide training and a support contact
tips.body: At rollout, provide an operating manual, internal briefing, frequently asked questions, and a support contact to reduce staff uncertainty.
points: Training for the first users
A documented FAQ
A contact for assistance
Support immediately after operations begin

tips.title: Define a post-launch improvement cycle
tips.body: Actual operations may reveal issues that were not visible immediately after rollout. Design the process around regular reviews.
points: Identify screens that take too long to complete
Review features that are not being used
Find operations that have reverted to manual work
Add fields needed for aggregation and reports

itAdvisor.governanceTitle: Data and production environments are handled with clear ownership.
itAdvisor.governanceLead: We align the service-page boundaries with the contract and do not operate with ambiguous permissions or external-service responsibilities.
governance: Domains, servers, cloud services, and similar resources are contracted under the customer's name in principle.
If a proxy contract is required, costs, incident responsibilities, cancellation, and ownership transfer are defined in an individual agreement, and work does not begin before agreement.
We avoid shared IDs and lending owner accounts. We use dedicated invitations and time-limited, least-privilege access, and enable multi-factor authentication where supported.
At completion, permissions are removed and, where necessary, secrets are revoked or rotated before handover.
AI services are agreed for each project according to data classification and contract terms and are not added or changed without permission.

Before handling confidential or personal information, we confirm whether it is used for training, where and how long it is stored, how it is deleted, and what must not be entered. It is not entered into any unapproved environment.
Production changes are made only after sharing the target and details and receiving the customer's approval.
When permission management, approval flows, or audit logs are required, they are included in the design scope, and we record the work target, changes, results, and handover items.
AI output is reviewed by a person, and the customer makes the final business decision.

itAdvisor.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions before consulting us
itAdvisor.faqLead: Even if you have not decided what to build, we can start by organizing the current workflow and what is blocking progress.

faqs.question: Can you launch code created with AI?
faqs.answer: After reviewing the architecture, dependencies, security, and operating conditions, we propose a launch method and any necessary changes. We never launch it unchanged without review.

faqs.question: Can we consult you even if we have not decided what to use AI for?
faqs.answer: Yes. We organize the workflow and present suitable candidates and priorities for AI and automation.

faqs.question: Might you recommend an approach that does not use AI?
faqs.answer: Yes. When conventional development, RPA, a database, or an existing service is more appropriate, we recommend that approach.

faqs.question: Does the monthly fee include development work?
faqs.answer: It includes work within the scope agreed in the contract for each plan. Full-scale new development and large system integrations are estimated separately.

faqs.question: Can we request deployment only?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-time support. The scope can cover recommended-environment selection, contracting support, initial setup, launch, and handover.

faqs.question: Who contracts the server and domain?
faqs.answer: In principle, they are contracted under the customer's name, and we support selection and setup. We do not take custody of shared IDs or owner accounts. The customer grants least-privilege access through a dedicated invitation or similar method, and we remove it on completion.

faqs.question: Can we also request day-to-day PC support?
faqs.answer: Help-desk work such as basic instruction and password resets is excluded. We cover adoption decisions, implementation, operational design, and technical second opinions.

faqs.question: Do you guarantee time savings or AI accuracy?
faqs.answer: No. We estimate them from the current state, then verify and improve them through a PoC and real operations.

itAdvisor.ctaTitle: Tell us what you built, what you are unsure about, and where progress has stopped.
itAdvisor.ctaBody: Launching a tool built with AI, adopting AI in operations, or deciding on server and IT architecture. In the initial consultation, we organize the problem and scope. If code investigation, environment diagnosis, or hands-on work is required, we begin after providing an estimate.

website.offeringsTitle: Website plans and flexible post-launch support
website.offeringsLead: Website production is priced as a one-time project, while monthly support is a separate agreement you can choose as needed. All prices include tax. Domain, server, paid-service, and other third-party costs are billed separately at cost. We’ll provide a quote for the confirmed scope and price before you sign.

Page planning for your company or shop introduction, services and pricing, directions, and more
Copy organization based on the facts, text, and photos you provide
Mobile-friendly design, editable announcements, basic SEO, and a contact form
Publishing and guidance on how to make updates, plus up to 2 rounds of consolidated content and design revisions
offerings.priceNote: A news listing, article detail pages, and a standard privacy notice are included separately from the static-page count. New interviews, photography, and custom design are quoted separately.

offerings.title: Enhanced & Redesign Plan
offerings.body: For those who want to showcase their services and examples, or rethink their website’s content and structure.
includes: Up to 10 static pages based on a standard structure, including a contact page
Interviews and draft copy and page structure within the agreed scope
Page planning tailored to your goals, such as service details, case studies, and recruitment information
The same core features as the Launch Plan, plus guidance on publishing and making updates
Up to 2 rounds of consolidated content and design revisions
offerings.priceNote: Migration of existing pages, articles, images, or URLs is scoped separately after we review the quantity and condition. Interviews and photography are not included.

offerings.title: Custom Design & Feature Add-ons
offerings.body: If you need a design tailored to your business or features such as booking and payments, we’ll start by clarifying your goals and how you plan to operate the site.
includes: Custom design, booking, payment, and membership features
Multilingual websites or migration of a large number of pages and articles
Review of your existing website structure and recommendations for necessary additional features
offerings.priceNote: We’ll provide an individual quote after confirming the features, third-party services, data requirements, and operating approach.

offerings.title: Maintenance Plan
offerings.body: For those who will update their own content but want regular technical checks taken care of.
includes: Automated uptime checks, backups, and regular inspections
Initial troubleshooting of issues and restoration from backups agreed in advance
Up to 30 minutes per month in total for inspections, troubleshooting, restoration, and related communication

offerings.title: Managed Updates Plan
offerings.body: For those who want a single point of contact for changes to business hours, pricing, photos, and announcements.
includes: Maintenance Plan coverage (up to 30 minutes per month)
Replacing copy or images on existing pages and publishing announcements
Up to 60 minutes per month for updates, including review, communication, confirmation requests, and publishing (up to 90 minutes per month combined with maintenance)
offerings.priceNote: New pages, design changes, new features, and long-form original copy are quoted separately. You provide the photos and factual information to be published.

offerings.title: Ongoing Improvement Plan
offerings.body: For those who want to make gradual improvements to their presentation and user pathways based on visitor activity, in addition to regular updates.
includes: Maintenance and updates to copy, images, and announcements
Review of website analytics and identification of improvement opportunities
Page improvements and consultations within the agreed scope
Up to 3 hours per month combined for maintenance, updates, analysis, consultations, and related communication
offerings.priceNote: Analysis begins after the required tracking setup is in place. Ad management, ongoing article production, and major overhauls are quoted separately.

website.termsTitle: Know what’s included before you get started

terms.title: Production scope and revision rounds
terms.body: Before work begins, we’ll agree on the page structure, content, delivery date, and price. The initial content and design review includes up to 2 rounds of consolidated revisions. Pages or structural changes added after the structure is approved will be quoted separately before work begins.

terms.title: Monthly work allowance
terms.body: Reviews and communication count toward each plan’s time allowance, and unused time does not carry over to the next month. Before starting work that exceeds the limit, we’ll confirm the scope, cost, and timing.

terms.title: Response and work schedule
terms.body: We aim to send an initial response within 2 business days. Completion dates for revisions are coordinated based on the request and available work time. Same-day service, 24-hour staffed monitoring, and emergency response are not included.

terms.title: Continuing support and cancellation
terms.body: There is no minimum contract term for monthly support. As a general rule, if you contact us by the 20th of the month, support ends at the end of that month; if you contact us on or after the 21st, it ends at the end of the following month. No prorated refunds are given for cancellations mid-month. We’ll confirm the applicable terms before you sign.

terms.title: Your data and handover
terms.body: Where possible, domains and external accounts will be set up in your name. When support ends, we’ll provide your copy and images, along with the website source code and exported data specified in the agreement. We’ll confirm in advance whether external services can be transferred and whether third-party licenses apply. Migration to a different hosting or publishing destination is quoted separately.

website.faqsTitle: Frequently asked questions about website design and updates

faqs.question: Can I work with you if I don’t run a shop or teaching studio?
faqs.answer: Yes. We work with small businesses, shops, teaching studios, and other organizations across all industries. We’ll make recommendations based on the information you need to share and how you plan to update the site.

faqs.question: Can we talk even if I don’t have all the copy or photos ready?
faqs.answer: Yes. For the Launch Plan, we organize the copy based on the facts and materials you provide. If you’d like us to draft copy based on interviews, we’ll define the scope under the Enhanced & Redesign Plan. Interviews and photography are quoted separately.

faqs.question: Can I hire you just to build a website or just to handle updates?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can hire us for production only. For maintenance or updates to an existing site, we’ll review its structure and access permissions and quote any initial setup work that may be needed.

faqs.question: Will my search ranking or number of inquiries increase?
faqs.answer: We set up basic SEO and easy-to-use pathways, but we can’t guarantee search rankings, traffic, sales, or the number of inquiries. We’ll consider improvements based on the data available.

faqs.question: Are CMS, SEO, and contact form fees charged separately?
faqs.answer: The standard CMS for announcements, basic SEO, and contact form are included in the production fee, with no separate feature charges. Additional features listed separately are quoted based on scope when your requirements go beyond the standard package.

cases.title: Improving the inquiry journey on the Acecore corporate site
cases.summary: We organized fixed pages, FAQs, AI chat, and CMS-managed fields to reduce uncertainty around service selection, estimates, and making contact.
cases.challenge: Visitors had difficulty knowing what they could discuss, and inquiry details were easily fragmented.
cases.proposal: We combined service-specific journeys, inquiry categories, FAQs, and AI guidance to collect the necessary information in the form.
cases.result: Separating pre-consultation guidance from formal inquiries made it easier to proceed to an estimate or service discussion.
cases.imageAlt: Contact page on the Acecore corporate site

cases.title: Acecore Store planning and development
cases.summary: We built an on-demand storefront that brings the journey from browsing official Acecore and Aceserver goods through cart, shipping confirmation, payment, manufacturing, and delivery into one coherent flow.
cases.challenge: Merchandise sales needed to keep inventory risk low while clearly presenting prices, shipping, returns, and seller information, and reliably connecting payment with manufacturing and delivery.
cases.proposal: Using Astro and Cloudflare Pages / Pages Functions, we combined D1, R2, Queues, Turnstile, Stripe Checkout, and the Printful API. Customers can confirm shipping and their total from the cart, then proceed from payment completion to manufacturing and delivery.
cases.result: We launched a sales foundation where customers can browse goods by Acecore and Aceserver brand and each order is sent for on-demand manufacturing. Payment information is not retained by the store, making it safer and easier to operate.
cases.imageAlt: Acecore Store home page featuring official Acecore and Aceserver goods

cases.title: Feature enhancements and operational foundation for the Acecore corporate site
cases.summary: We progressively added a CMS, article foundation, site search, structured data, CSP, accessibility improvements, and performance improvements to a static site.
cases.challenge: The architecture needed to strengthen publishing and inquiry journeys without sacrificing the speed or operability of the static site.
cases.proposal: We combined Astro, Cloudflare Pages, Sveltia CMS, Pagefind, structured data, and security headers in a structure where required features can be added incrementally.
cases.result: The resulting foundation allows blogs, fixed pages, search, and inquiry journeys to be operated and improved, and produced reusable knowledge for similar site-enhancement projects.
cases.imageAlt: Home page of the Acecore corporate site

cases.title: Stability and monitoring knowledge gained from Aceserver operations
cases.summary: Through operating a public Minecraft server, we continuously improve connection stability, monitoring, backups, and guidance journeys.
cases.challenge: As participation grows, connection stability, information sharing, incident response, and operational rules require more structure.
cases.proposal: Instead of separating technical and community operations, we improved the server architecture, monitoring, backups, and Web journeys together.
cases.result: Knowledge from long-term operations can now inform monitoring and operational design for business systems.
cases.imageAlt: Main screen of the Aceserver portal

cases.title: Aceserver portal development
cases.category: Web production, community portal, and CMS
cases.summary: We organized participation guidance, videos, world maps, Wiki, and Discord links for the free public Minecraft server Aceserver into one entry point.
cases.challenge: Information about the server, how to join, rules, videos, and world maps was spread across multiple locations, making the first step unclear for new visitors.
cases.proposal: Without replacing existing information sources, we built a portal that guides visitors from the server introduction to Discord, videos, each world map, and the Wiki.
cases.result: It is published as a static site using Astro, UnoCSS, and Sveltia CMS. Page content and site settings can be updated through the CMS.
cases.imageAlt: Home page of the Aceserver portal

cases.title: Cherry English School site renewal
cases.category: Web production, CMS, and site search
cases.summary: We organized school information, courses, announcements, blogs, events, and FAQs into one site and renewed the existing site with an Astro architecture.
cases.challenge: The new structure needed to preserve the existing site and blog content while helping visitors proceed to courses and trial lessons and allowing updates to continue.
cases.proposal: We combined Astro, UnoCSS, Sveltia CMS, and Pagefind into one operating foundation covering existing-article migration, legacy URL redirects, site search, and CMS updates.
cases.result: Visitors can more easily find school information, trial lessons, daily announcements, and older articles, while CMS changes can be reviewed in a PR before publication.
cases.imageAlt: Home page of the Cherry English School website
cases.externalLabel: View the Cherry English School website

cases.title: Hatt website development
cases.category: Web production, CMS, and site search
cases.summary: We brought illustrations, novels, and 3D avatar and gimmick production for VRChat into one entry point, designing a personal site for ongoing creative publishing.
cases.challenge: Entry points were split among a blog, external publishing sites, BOOTH, YouTube, X, and other services, making it hard for first-time visitors to understand the full scope or viewing order.
cases.proposal: We organized the work into 3 areas—illustration, novels, and modeling—and built a hub linking the blog, works, profile, and external services.
cases.result: It is published as a static site using Astro, TypeScript, UnoCSS, Sveltia CMS, and Pagefind. Blogs and work information can be updated through the CMS, and articles and works are searchable.
